title: The Ailing Planet: The Green Movement’s Role
subject: English

notes.heading: Theme
notes.text: The text focuses on the deteriorating health of the Earth caused by human over-exploitation, shifting human perception to a holistic ecological view, and advocating for sustainable development to protect future generations.

summary: "The Ailing Planet: the Green Movement's Role" by Nani Palkhivala is a thought-provoking commentary that addresses the deteriorating health of the Earth caused by reckless human exploitation and highlights the crucial need for global environmental conservation. Originally published as an article in 1994, it explains how the Green Movement, launched in New Zealand in 1972, triggered a monumental shift in human perception from a narrow mechanical view to a holistic, ecological worldview. Humans began recognizing the Earth not merely as a resource base but as a living organism whose declining vital signs indicate a patient in desperate need of healing. To emphasize the gravity of human destruction, the author references a sign at a zoo in Lusaka, Zambia, which declares human beings as the "world's most dangerous animal" by placing a mirror inside an empty cage. The text introduces the concept of sustainable development, popularized in 1987, which advocates for fulfilling contemporary needs without stripping future generations of their ability to survive. Palkhivala warns that the planet's four principal biological systems—fisheries, forests, grasslands, and croplands—which form the entire foundation of the global economic system, are reaching unsustainable thresholds. Deforestation is rampant, soil productivity is collapsing, and the alarming rate of world overpopulation acts as the single biggest factor distorting the future of human society. The author asserts that development is the best contraceptive to curb fertility rates, yet proper development is impossible if population numbers continue to surge unchecked. Ultimately, the essay calls for a new "Era of Responsibility," reminding us of the wisdom popularized by Lester Brown that we have not inherited this Earth from our ancestors; rather, we have borrowed it from our children and bear a moral lease to pass it on in a healthy, habitable condition.

qa.q: Locate the lines in the text that support the title “The Ailing Planet”.
qa.a: The title is supported by the references to the declining health of the earth. The text mentions the destruction of forests, loss of species, pollution and the depletion of natural resources. These problems show that the earth is like an ailing planet that needs immediate care.

qa.q: What does the notice “The world’s most dangerous animal” at a cage in the zoo at Lusaka, Zambia, signify?
qa.a: The notice refers to human beings as the world’s most dangerous animal. Humans have caused widespread destruction of forests, wildlife and natural resources. Their careless activities have endangered the environment and many other species.

qa.q: How are the earth’s principal biological systems being depleted?
qa.a: The earth’s biological systems are being depleted through excessive human activities. Forests are being destroyed, fisheries are being overused, grasslands are being damaged and croplands are losing their fertility. These activities reduce the earth’s ability to support life.

qa.q: Why does the author say that the environmental problem is not a temporary one?
qa.a: The environmental problem is not temporary because human activities are continuously damaging the earth’s natural systems. Population growth, pollution, deforestation and excessive use of resources are long-term problems. If they continue, they will seriously affect future generations.

qa.q: How do the earth’s principal biological systems sustain humanity?
qa.a: The earth’s biological systems provide humans with food, water, clean air and other essential resources. Forests, fisheries, grasslands and croplands support human life by providing food and maintaining ecological balance. Human survival depends on these systems.

qa.q: How do you think the concept of sustainable development has been introduced in the text?
qa.a: The text introduces sustainable development by stressing that natural resources must be used carefully. Development should meet the needs of the present without destroying resources needed by future generations. It calls for a balance between development and environmental protection.

qa.q: Explain the concept of “holistic and ecological view of the world”.
qa.a: A holistic and ecological view means seeing the earth as a complete system in which all living things are connected. Humans, animals, plants and natural resources depend on one another. Therefore, protecting nature is necessary for the survival and well-being of humanity.
